newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian gov't concedes fiscal deficit soaring.
newsitem.headline: Colombian gov't concedes fiscal deficit soaring.

text.p: The fiscal deficit of Colombia's central government is expected to total 3.97 percent of gross domestic product by year end, well above the government's original target of 3.27 percent, the finance ministry said.

A ministry source, who spoke on condition that he would not be identified by name, said the deficit had mushroomed because of an unexpected drop in tax revenues and because of the burgeoning cost of servicing the government's internal debt. Interest payments on the internal debt total 1.28 percent of GDP so far this year, up from 0.73 percent in 1995, the source told Reuters.

The central government's fiscal deficit totalled 2.85 trillion pesos, or 3.19 percent of GDP, at the end of October, according to official finance ministry figures. This compares with a deficit equal to 1.57 percent of GDP during the first 10 months of 1995.

"We're going to close the year at nearly 4.0 percent," said the source, who said his estimate was based on the successful privatization, by January 1, of the state-run bank Banco Popular and several power plants due to hit the auction block by year-end.

The finance ministry figures show that the government expects to earn 200 billion pesos from privatizations this year, down significantly from the 2.7 trillion pesos that it earned from the selloff of state-run businesses and industries in 1996.

The drop in tax revenues so far this year, which have fallen by 700 billion pesos or nearly 1.0 percent of GDP compared with the first 10 months of 1995, was attributed by the finance ministry source to Colombia's sharp economic slowdown during the first nine months of 1996.
